archivist.text: Blackthorn House: unoccupied for forty years, according to the record. Yet a lamp burns upstairs. Your invitation bears tomorrow's date and your own handwriting. I would preserve that discrepancy. The door closes. A brass key, a girl's defaced portrait, small bare footprints in the dust. Behind the walls, something counts backward. 'Observe before you touch,' I tell you. A house is an archive. Someone has been removing the names.

medium.text: There is a child here. Blackthorn House has stood empty for forty years, but her waiting fills it. A lamp burns upstairs. Your invitation carries tomorrow's date, written in your own hand. 'Stay where you can hear me,' I whisper as the door closes. A brass key rests beside a girl's portrait; someone has wounded the paint where her name should be. Small bare footprints disturb the dust. Something counts backward in the walls. I feel her flinch at every number.

skeptic.text: Working hypothesis: somebody wants to frighten you. Blackthorn House has been empty for forty years, but a lamp is on. Your invitation has tomorrow's date and your handwriting. A forgery, presumably. The door shuts. On the table are a brass key and a girl's portrait with the name scratched out; small bare footprints cross the dust. Something counts backward inside the walls. 'Pipes,' I say. 'Or a recording. We check the evidence, then we leave.'
